title: Конец утренним пробежкам  (An End to Morning Jogs)

segments.t: Relieved by Elena's honesty, Viktor Petrovich confesses in turn that he staged the urgent phone call from Lyova during their first run because he was about to pass out. Laughing together at their mutual pride, the two rival chefs happily shake hands on a pact: no more sports from this moment on.
Я вообще думаю, что вы откажетесь.
А со звонком вы здорово придумали.
С этого момента больше никакого спорта.
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
Я вообще думаю, что вы откажетесь.

'I honestly thought that you would refuse.' Mentioning that he honestly thought that Nastya would refuse moves the talk in a new direction. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
А со звонком вы здорово придумали.

'And that phone call trick you came up with was brilliant.' Nastya reminds Kostya that that phone call trick Kostya came up with was brilliant before the moment passes. Notice how she sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
'All right, I will be right there.' Because all right he will be right there, Kostya treats the matter as settled.

'Are you really leaving already, huh?' By asking whether Kostya really leaving already huh, Nastya presses Kostya for a straight answer. In Russian, she does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.

'What happened?' With the conversation and point hanging in the air, Kostya puts Nastya on the spot. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
'Yes, they are urgently calling me in to work.' Because they are urgently calling her in to work, Nastya treats the matter as settled.

'Well then, tomorrow at the same place?' Over the point and the phone, Kostya presses Nastya for a straight answer. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
'At the exact same time?' Around the point and pride, Nastya wants to know where Kostya really stands. Russian drops "is" in the present, setting the two halves of the thought side by side.
'Well, see you tomorrow.' Seeing Nastya tomorrow is how Kostya lays out the situation for Nastya.
'Thank you for the company.' Over the conversation and the morning, Nastya answers Kostya without a second thought.

'All right, let us make a deal.' Even though all right let them make a deal, Kostya keeps a steady face in front of Nastya. Starting with "davay" is the everyday Russian way to say "come on, let us do this".
С этого момента больше никакого спорта.
'From this moment on, no more sports.' With the conversation and call in play, Nastya keeps this short reply brisk and direct.
'I could not be happier to agree.' Saying that he could not be happier to agree is how Kostya sets the tone with Nastya. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.
Я вообще думаю, что вы откажетесь.
А со звонком вы здорово придумали.
С этого момента больше никакого спорта.

That wraps up this scene as chef Barinov confesses to Elena that he faked the urgent work call from Lyova to escape their first run, and the two chefs happily agree to give up sports forever. See you next time!
